newsitem.title: USA: Pluma says Q2 to be lower than expected.
newsitem.headline: Pluma says Q2 to be lower than expected.

text.p: Pluma Inc said Monday that the expected gain in earnings for the second quarter compared to a year ago will be "somewhat less than anticipated."
The company reported net sales of $33.9 million and net income of $641,000, or $0.12 per share, in the second quarter of 1996.

R. Duke Ferrell, president and chief executive officer, said that Plum had completed the reconfiguration of its textile operations, including relocation of the knitting, greige fabrics and cutting departments in Eden, N.C.
"While the reconfiguration is now complete, it caused some delays in the production and shipment of orders during the quarter, particularly the latter part of June," he said.
As a result, he said, the company's second quarter sales will be approximately $33 million to $33.5 million, slightly below last year's record level.

He said that to help bring the company back on schedule, it has begun implementing a plan which includes operating most of its facilities during the week of July 4th, traditionally a vacation week for the industry.
The company still expected the majority of our sales and earnings for 1997 to be generated during the second half of the year, he said.
